dedupe_keys.name: sorghum supply development in meru county kenya netlogo agent based model of contracts and trust between smallholders and a processor

description: This NetLogo model assesses a project that developed sorghum production and marketing in Meru County, Kenya, as part of inclusive business that brings low-income communities into value chains. It was written by Tim Verwaart and Coen van Wagenberg and published in the CoMSES library (version 1.1.0, 2019). Contracts between a local sorghum processor and smallholders are central, and trust between farmers and the processor, and within farmer groups, is a key factor in whether supply becomes stable. The simulation is combined with games as an impact assessment tool that measures changes in farm income, transaction costs and behaviour in value chain relationships. The code is available as a free download from CoMSES under the AFL-3.0 licence. Caveats: it is tied to one project and region. Coverage is Meru County, Kenya. Simulation uses: testing how contract and trust arrangements secure supply to local food processors. Related records: the soy value chain model for northern Ghana (model-comses-soy-value-chains-northern-ghana), by the same author, applies the approach to soy.
